newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schaeuble sees chance for tax compromise.
newsitem.headline: Schaeuble sees chance for tax compromise.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition will continue to press its tax reform agenda, and sees a chance for agreement with the opposition, said Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of the Christian Democrats (CDU).

The Social Democrat-dominated mediation committee's rejection of the government's programme does not mean that tax reform is dead, Schaeuble said in an interview with the newspaper Die Welt published on Tuesday.
"The outcome of a second mediation process is completely open," Schaeuble said. "I would put the odds of success in social security premiums at over 50 percent."

The SPD also recognises the need for tax reform and to cut tax rates, he said. The example of U.S. tax cuts, and criticism from other countries of Germany's failure to reform will make it difficult not to change, he said.

"It would simply be better to pull ourselves together," he said. Coalition parties in the lower house voted on Tuesday to press for a second mediation process on tax reform in autumn, but the SPD has vowed to kill it again.

Schaeuble said the net tax cuts may not be as large as the 30 billion marks initially foreseen by the government, but both the minimum and maximum tax rates for individuals, and corporate tax rates, must be cut.
The coalition is firm in its decision that the solidarity income tax surcharge will be cut two percentage points in January 1998, but counter-financing will be needed, he said.
